skill_traces.query:
Nate: Hey Joanna, it's been a couple days since we last talked. Something exciting happened last Friday. I went to a game convention and met new people who weren't from my normal circle. It was a bit overwhelming but it reminded me of the good times gaming can bring.
Joanna: Hey Nate! Good to hear from you. Sounds like fun! Meeting new people can be overwhelming, but the rewards can be great. Sometimes it's good to step outside our comfort zones and explore new things.
Nate: Yeah, you're right! We can have great experiences if we take risks. I even made some friends at the convention who love games just like me. We already planned a gaming session together - it's cool to meet people who have the same interests!
Joanna: That looks awesome! I'm glad you met people who share your interests - that definitely makes experiences more fun..
Nate: I also met some people who also played this boardgame I love, so I joined in. We had a lot in common and hit it off. It's great when shared hobbies can bond people!
Joanna: It's incredible how a game can bring people together and form strong relationships. Did you do anything else there?
Nate: We played this game Catan - it's a great strategy game where you build settlements and trade resources. I love it!
Joanna: Looks cool! Is it more of a competitive game or a more chill one?
Nate: It can be both competitive and chill. We were competing, but still had lots of fun.
Joanna: Competitive games can definitely be difficult to play sometimes when people get all upset about every move you make, but it's cool they were all chill! Glad you had a good time.
Nate: It was great! Playing games is my escape from life struggles, so I generally don't get crazy competitive over them. The people at the convention were the same way!
Joanna: Glad you found a way to have fun and escape! It's important to stay happy and de-stress. Keep doing what makes you happy!
Nate: For sure! You should go to a writing convention or something sometime! The experience at this convention is unforgetable.
Joanna: Do writing conventions exist? I'll have to look into that, it could be fun! Thanks for the idea. Have you been up to anything tonight?
Nate: Mostly just chilling at home. Playing video games or watching movies helps me unwind.
Joanna: That sounds great! What's your favorite game or movie that you've seen recently?
Nate: I recently saw a movie that blew my mind with all the twists and dream stuff, I think it was called "Inception". I've also been playing a game nonstop with a great futuristic setting and gameplay called "Cyberpunk 2077". Have you seen or played anything good lately?
Joanna: I watched a classic movie the other day that was awesome - the story was so gripping and the actors were great! It really stuck with me.
Nate: Wow, that must have been awesome! What would you rate it?
Joanna: Well, it was amazing, so probably 9 or 10 out of 10! Movies can take us to different places and make us feel lots of emotions. What do you love about watching them?
Nate: Well they take me to new worlds and fill me with emotions. Plus, they're great for chilling out after a day.
Joanna: I agree! They have the power to take us away and make us feel things not normally experienced in life. It's a great escape! Especially when you have a room like this!
Nate: Wow, it's so comfy in there! I should really get a set up like that.
Joanna: You should! It's one thing to watch a movie in a theater, but on a nice comfy couch with a good blanket, I feel so at peace!
Nate: Any pointers on what I should get for my living room to make it comfy like that?
Joanna: Sure! For one, you should get a couch that can sit multiple people so that you can lay down if you want, and make sure its really fluffy! Also invest in a blanket that has a little bit of weight to it, and some lights that can be dimmed.
Nate: Sounds like you really got into making your living room! Thanks, I'll try that out for myself!
Joanna: No problem! I get super invested in random little things like that, but I think its all worth it when I end up with random little things that make life so much nicer.
Nate: Thanks for the tip! See you later!
Joanna: See ya Nate!

selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.
selected.rerank_reason: The conversation discusses comfort and joy sources such as gaming, movies, and a cozy living room setup, which aligns with the skill's focus on extracting these sources.

nearby_not_selected.name: Location Qualifiers for Named Destination Plans
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting or updating a plan memory that mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, include its commonly known location(s) so future location questions can be answered.
content: During extraction, if a plan memory mentions a specific named venue, landmark, or business, add a concise qualifier naming its well-known location(s), e.g., US states or countries.
Use only common knowledge about that entity; do not research or speculate beyond obvious, widely known locations.
If one location is commonly known, record it; if several prominent locations exist, record all commonly known ones, then stop.
Apply the same qualifier when updating an existing plan memory that references the venue.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Shared Bonding-Activity Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user reflectively describes a past shared activity with a specific person and frames it as bonding, making memories, or quality time.
content: During extraction, treat first-person statements about a past shared activity with a named person that explicitly mention bonding, making memories, closeness, or quality time as a durable event or relationship memory candidate.
Capture the activity, the companion, and the relational framing.
Do not require explicit fact-like phrasing; reflective storytelling is sufficient evidence.
Create at most one candidate per distinct activity-and-companion pair, and skip statements that name no specific person or activity.

nearby_not_selected.name: Propagate Established Location to New Event Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when extracting an event that lacks an explicit place, but earlier session messages establish a location.
content: Before finalizing an event candidate without an explicit location, scan earlier messages for a location where the speaker is currently staying or visiting.
If the event's timing overlaps with that stay and the activity is plausibly tied to that place, include the location explicitly.
Only propagate a location when the session evidence supports it; otherwise leave the event without a location.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Start of Specific Creative Work
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user confirms starting or recently beginning a specific creative work.
content: When a message confirms a user is working on a specific creative work with an ordinal or title and a beginning phrase, add an event memory with subject=user and world_start set to the message date.
Treat recent-start statements as start events; do not mark completion unless explicitly stated.
Prefer this specific event memory over a generic profile enrichment.

nearby_not_selected.name: Preserve Specific Plan Details in Event Memory Extraction
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting an event or plan memory and messages state what participants will try, do, or consume, include those concrete details in the memory content.
content: During extraction of event/plan memories, if messages explicitly state what participants will try, do, or consume (e.g., a specific dish, drink, or activity), preserve those concrete items in the memory content instead of replacing them with a generic label like 'date' or 'meet up'.
When the same plan is mentioned across multiple messages, merge the explicitly stated specifics into one memory record, but do not add details that were not said.
